findings.title: Evaluate invalidation against stored enabled state, not organization-aware state
findings.body: The original model passed to this method comes from getById(), which wraps isEnabled() to return false when the organization or organization support is disabled. The login query, however, caches IDs using the delegate's stored enabled flag. If a public, enabled organization's IDP is cached, the organization is disabled, and the IDP is then hidden on login or made link-only, both predicates here return false and invalidation is skipped. After the organization is re-enabled, the cached ID is still returned; OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only rechecks isEnabled(), so the hidden/link-only provider appears on the login page. Compare the original persisted login-filter fields without the organization-aware enabled override.

findings.title: Do not republish old query results using a fresh startup revision
findings.body: When adding an uncached organization search, this branch copies all existing searches from query and publishes them using cache.getCurrentCounter() after the database query. An IDP change can invalidate the login cache between reading query and publishing the replacement. The fresh counter allows the replacement to pass the revision check despite containing pre-invalidation search results (and potentially stale database results). This can resurrect lists that omit newly available providers or include providers that have been hidden or made private. Use a revision captured before reading/loading the results and avoid copying a query invalidated in the meantime.

findings.title: Register cleanup for the actual created IDP aliases
findings.body: The test creates providers named idp-alias-0 through idp-alias-19, but every cleanup callback removes the literal provider name "alias" instead. The additional callback at line 425 repeats the same mistake for idp-alias-20. Consequently these providers are not cleaned up, and cleanup may fail with a not-found response; leftover realm-level providers can also contaminate subsequent tests. Register each callback with the alias of the provider it created.
